subject: Urgent: Kepler AI — sudden 5xx/429 surge after kepler-2026q4 rollout
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@kepler-ai.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ops@kepler-ai.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Production surge: 5xx/429 spike after model switchover

Hi Stephanie —

We flipped Kepler AI traffic over to your kepler-2026q4 model at ~08:48 PDT. Within ten minutes we started seeing a large uptick in 5xx and 429 responses from your API for our inference path (session-based chat endpoint). Our side shows an immediate increase in client retries which appears to have amplified error rates and latency across our service mesh. Snapshot: 08:55–09:05 we saw 5xx go from 0.2% → 6.3% and 429 from 0.1% → 4.1%.

Attached are a few error samples and a short trace segment. Impact: several critical user flows in our app are timing out (30s). Can Redwood pause or roll back the new model? We need an urgent mitigation plan and ETA. 

Thanks — please escalate as needed.

— Sarah
Sarah Liu
SRE Lead, Kepler AI

Attachments: kepler_error_samples.log, trace_segment_10-12.jsonl
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@kepler-ai.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production surge: 5xx/429 spike after model switchover

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for the logs. We see the anomaly on our side as well (alerts triggered at 08:52 PDT).

Immediate actions:
- We are pausing further rollout of kepler-2026q4 to other regions.
- As a short-term mitigation we can flip your routing to the previous pinned model (kepler-2026q3-stable) within ~12 minutes if you approve. That will remove the new quant+kernel path causing instability.
- Marcus is investigating whether the new kernel selection is hitting a corner-case that thrashes KV cache and triggers backpressure leading to 429s (we've seen similar signatures in internal tests).

Can you confirm you'd like us to roll traffic back to kepler-2026q3 for your account? If you prefer a canary-only rollback first, we can route 100% of your traffic to the stable variant for 30 minutes and monitor.

I'll loop in our exec app owner and PM for priority.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Customer Escalations, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Kernel/caching hypothesis + quick mitigations

Stephanie / Marissa — quick notes from initial triage:
- Symptom: spike in 5xx (503s) + 429s immediately after the kepler-2026q4 kernel selection changed on the host pool that serves Kepler AI.
- Telemetry: KV cache hit ratio dropped ~42% and mem pressure rose briefly on the affected hosts; per-token latency for long-context sessions doubled for requests that used persistent sessions (KV reuse).
- Hypothesis: a kernel scheduling path in kernel-Xv2 used for kepler-2026q4 interacts poorly with our async KV eviction logic under certain sequence-length distributions. The result is transient resource contention, request queue growth, and token-generation failures that return 5xx; upstream client retries then produce 429s as worker pools throttle.

Immediate mitigation options (ranked):
1) Roll back Kepler AI to kepler-2026q3-stable (fastest, low risk).
2) Apply a canary patch to disable the new kernel-Xv2 path and force kernel-Xv1 for affected hosts (requires 10–15m rollout). Patch diff attached (canary_switch_patch.diff).
3) Short-term rate-limit inbound concurrency for Kepler AI at edge (50% of normal) to reduce amplification while we fix the kernel.

I'm working on a quick script to run a targeted revert and gather deeper flamegraphs — will post results in 20 minutes.

— Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: canary_switch_patch.diff
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@kepler-ai.com>, ops@kepler-ai.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production surge: 5xx/429 spike after model switchover — proposed rollback plan

Sarah — following internal triage, recommended plan:
1) Immediate: Flip Kepler AI routing to kepler-2026q3-stable (full rollback for your traffic). We can do this at 09:05 PDT and monitor for 30 minutes. Estimated service window: 09:05–09:15 (flip + stabilization).
2) Concurrent: Marcus will push the canary kernel switch on the small subset of affected hosts to validate the kernel-Xv2 interaction (non-disruptive, ~15m).
3) Post-stabilization: we'll run a 1-hour verification run and provide you full metrics and flamegraphs.

Please reply with APPROVE to proceed with the rollback. If you need us to coordinate a brief maintenance window with your ops team, say the word and we'll schedule the change.

We understand the customer impact and are treating this as an elevated incident (I have looped in Rishi for exec notification).

— Stephanie
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@kepler-ai.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ops@kepler-ai.com, ivan.kovacs@kepler-ai.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production surge: 5xx/429 spike after model switchover — proposed rollback plan

APPROVE. Please proceed with the full rollback to kepler-2026q3-stable now. Our CTO (Ivan) is on standby and will expect status updates. Thank you for the rapid response.

— Sarah
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@kepler-ai.com>, ops@kepler-ai.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Resolution: rollback complete + next steps

Sarah — rollback to kepler-2026q3-stable completed at 09:07 PDT for your account. Metrics update: by 09:12 PDT 5xx returned to baseline (~0.3%) and 429s dropped under 0.2%. We left a 15-minute canary window before restoring full traffic to validate stability.

Actions taken and artifacts attached:
- Traffic rollback executed (audit id: RB-20261012-KEP-001).
- Collected traces and heap snapshots from affected hosts; see drive link (related_links).
- Marcus ran flamegraphs and captured KV eviction traces; initial evidence supports kernel-Xv2 scheduling corner-case.

Next steps (proposed):
- 48h hotfix: either toggle kernel-Xv2 off for the affected hardware families or apply a scheduling patch. Marcus to own.
- Postmortem: 2026-10-13 10:00 PDT (30m) — propose joint review with Kepler AI to review root cause and preventative controls.
- We will produce a short executive summary for Ivan/your CTO by EOD.

I'll keep you posted on the hotfix timeline. Really sorry for the disruption and thank you for the quick sign-off.

— Stephanie

Attachments: latency_graph_20261012.png, kepler_error_samples.log
